claims.text: The target domain consists of 4–6-principal-element high-entropy alloys in solid and liquid states from approximately 0.8 Tm through complete melting.
Traditional TOR–TILD EAM references inadequately represent the many atomic configurations of high-temperature multicomponent liquids.
Traditional EAM references are the current state of the art for the specified thermodynamic-integration workflow.
An actively learned deep neural-network potential trained on ab initio solid and liquid configurations will represent the target HEA configurations more faithfully than an EAM reference.
A DeepMD potential has been trained on DFT calculations to describe both solid and liquid phases of high-entropy carbonitrides, with active learning used in the melting-temperature procedure.
The flexible data-driven potential captures many-body interactions and local-coordination variations in both solid and liquid phases.
Active learning targets atomic configurations that are underrepresented in the training data.
The actively learned potential will accurately reproduce the ab initio energy landscape of multicomponent HEAs near melting.
More accurate representation of diverse configurations will improve reference–target phase-space overlap.
Improved phase-space overlap will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR–TILD EAM references.
The deep-learning reference will produce free-energy differences agreeing with ab initio benchmarks within their nominal uncertainty.
The deep-learning reference will provide statistically significant improvements in configurational sampling and energy accuracy over the EAM reference.
The method is applicable primarily to alloys with 4–6 principal elements near melting.
The method may perform poorly for alloys with chemical complexity beyond the stated 4–6-element regime.
Insufficient diversity in the ab initio training set may prevent the potential from capturing all relevant configurations.
Prior elemental and binary calculations support applying deep-learning interatomic potentials to this problem.
High-entropy-carbonitride calculations provide evidence that a DFT-trained DeepMD potential can be used for solid–liquid melting studies.
The magnitude of the thermodynamic-integration improvement depends sensitively on the quality and diversity of the ab initio training data.
Direct ab initio free energies can serve as the decisive benchmark for comparing the deep-learning and EAM thermodynamic-integration workflows.
Failure to improve either the integration mismatch or phase-space-overlap metric relative to EAM would falsify the hypothesis.
